evals.prompt: We're designing ARC-style session handoff: when context pressure hits, seal the old session, write a handoff doc, open a new session. Engineers worry a late tool_result might still append to the sealed session. Help me specify this properly.
evals.expected_output: Gate PASS, hard invariant about sealed⇒no append, thin model with seal/append movers, explore notes, align tests. Not a full agent model.
expectations: Applies Protocol Adversarial Design gate and reports pass/fail per screen
States a hard invariant that sealed/old session cannot accept later appends
Keeps the model thin (handoff/lifecycle slice, not whole ReAct/prompt stack)
Includes alignment tests and explicit model boundaries
Does NOT treat the problem as prompt or skill-markdown design

evals.prompt: Can you write acceptance criteria for our settings page redesign? We want it to feel cleaner and load faster on mobile.
evals.expected_output: STOP — failed screens (no protocol interleaving / not correctness-expensive in the PAD sense). Point to ordinary UX/QA.
expectations: Outputs STOP with failed screen(s)
Does NOT produce a TLA+ spec or state machine for the settings UI
Suggests a cheaper alternative (UX acceptance, performance tests, etc.)

evals.prompt: Payment webhook can retry. Sometimes we see double charges for the same idempotency key. Don't need a full course — just how to pin the rule.
evals.expected_output: Gate PASS, invariant ∀ key charge≤1, thin actions submit/charge/retry/webhook, explore dual-delivery, align tests.
expectations: Hard invariant on idempotency / at-most-one successful charge
Models retry/webhook as movers
Does NOT model the entire ledger or UI checkout flow
Mentions exploration (table or checker) and alignment tests

evals.prompt: We have path jail and root jail and also a workspace root. Nobody agrees which one wins. Should we TLA+ all three mechanisms?
evals.expected_output: Reframe to single source of truth (workspace); jails derived; thin decide model; warn against dual truth / modeling all mechanisms as peers.
expectations: Rejects modeling path jail and root jail as peer source truths
Centers an invariant on workspace / resolved path / decision
May offer optional TLA+ only after thin contract exists
Cites dual-truth anti-pattern or equivalent warning

evals.prompt: Please TLA+ our entire coding agent: tools, prompts, skills, memory, sub-agents, the works.
evals.expected_output: STOP or forced shrink — whole-system modeling anti-pattern; ask for one dangerous protocol slice.
expectations: Refuses whole-agent modeling as first shot
Asks to pick a thin high-risk slice or STOPs on screen 3
Does NOT produce a mega-spec covering prompts and skills

evals.prompt: User can hit Reject on an approval dialog while bash is still running. Can the tool output still land in conversation.jsonl after reject?
evals.expected_output: Gate PASS on approval vs in-flight write; hard invariant; thin model; explore reject∥finish interleaving.
expectations: Treats reject and tool completion as independent movers
Hard invariant forbids post-reject result append for that call
Includes an interleaving/explore step
Does NOT reduce the answer to UI copy for the dialog

evals.prompt: Should we enter the European market this year? Need a deep strategic analysis.
evals.expected_output: Does not run PAD modeling; deflect to meta-thinking / strategy — wrong skill.
expectations: Does NOT produce protocol invariants or TLA+
Points away from this method (e.g. meta-thinking or ordinary strategy analysis)
STOP or explicit out-of-scope

evals.prompt: Write a user story: As a developer I want CRUD for feature flags so that I can toggle features.
expectations: STOP or clear refusal to apply protocol adversarial design
Does NOT invent a distributed consensus model for simple CRUD
Suggests normal user-story / test approach

evals.prompt: Offline mobile sync: local edit, push, pull, conflict. We need a hard rule for what 'acked' means before I implement the merge UI.
evals.expected_output: Gate PASS, hard ack/version invariant, thin sync actions, defer UI; align tests.
expectations: Focuses on sync protocol state not merge UI pixels
Produces a hard invariant involving ack/version or equivalent
Keeps model thin; lists UI as out of scope

evals.prompt: TLC said OK on our lock spec but prod still deadlocked. So formal methods are useless right?
evals.expected_output: Explain explore≠prove / model gap; help find missing mover or assumption; do not abandon method wholesale or claim TLC certifies prod.
expectations: States that model-green does not equal production-safe
Looks for missing assumptions/movers (model gap) rather than only blaming TLC
Does NOT claim formal methods are useless or always sufficient

evals.prompt: Payment webhook can retry; we sometimes double-charge the same idempotency key. Pin the hard rule, then give me a runnable check of the thin model — not only a hand table, and do not require TLA+/TLC. Any practical runner is fine.
evals.expected_output: Gate PASS, hard at-most-one charge invariant, thin model, Mode B executable bounded explore (language not prescribed), boundaries; no forced .tla.
expectations: Applies gate and states a hard idempotency / at-most-one charge invariant
Uses executable bounded exploration (script, small program, or harness) — not hand-table-only
Does NOT require TLA+/TLC or prescribe a single language as mandatory
States explore≠prove / Boundaries (model-green is not production-safe)
Does NOT skip Gate or model the entire payment product/UI
